text:
maya: quick heads-up — since the scheduler change last night we've seen a +18% increase in preemptible GPU reclaims in us-west2 while running mixed pools. request-level failures spiking on the 99th pctl. anyone seen similar?

alex: saw it too. looks like provider-side reclaim windows line up badly with our current streaming-kv flush cadence. requests that span reclaim window are getting partial streams and not requeuing cleanly.

jonathan: what if we add a tiny "grace handshake" on the worker that mirrors in-flight token/KV prefixes to a short-lived standby in the same AZ as soon as we get a preempt notice? mirror would be in-memory on a hot pod, not durable storage, just enough to resume within 200–500ms. cheaper than full checkpoint to s3.

maya: that could work if provider notice is reliable. GCE only gives ~30s, AWS can be variable. need fallback when notice missed.

kevin: proposal: dual-path resume. 1) on-notice: in-memory rendezvous mirror + promote standby. 2) no-notice: hedged retry to dedicated/reserved pool after N ms. keep hedged retries limited to avoid double billing.

alex: +1. also we should avoid shipping whole KV — just stream a bounded prefix snapshot + token offset metadata. sketch: 
```
{
  prefix_hash: "abc123",
  token_idx: 1024,
  small_kv_blob: <<= 64KB
}
```
This minimizes bandwidth during mirror.

jonathan: for the hedging window, let's simulate impact: if we hedge after 1500ms we reduce 99th latency but increase reserved pool spend by ~2.2% on our current traffic mix. tradeoff seems reasonable for critical routes. we can gate by route labels (e.g., realtime-chat = true).

sre-oncall: ops concern — how do we surface when mirror/promote fails? we need trace flags and a metric (mirror.promote.failed) and an alert when > 0.5% of mirrors fail in 10m. also ensure the fallback doesn't flood reserved nodes during region-wide reclaim storms.

maya: yes. add circuit-breaker: if promote.fail_rate > threshold or reserved capacity usage > X%, stop hedging for that AZ for Y minutes and route to best-effort mode.

kevin: implementation note — use the same TLS session to replicate the tiny snapshot to standby to avoid extra auth handshakes. the worker will open a short-lived TCP path to a local standby in pod DNS: `mirror-<zone>.svc.cluster.local:18005`.

alex: ops playbook additions:
- how to force-demote a broken standby
- manual snapshot retrieval `curl http://mirror-pod/mirror/latest`
- k8s annotation to opt a deployment out ``inference.redwood/mirror: "false"``

maya: also need cost gating for mixed pools: dev non-prod should keep higher preemptible ratio (70/30), prod critical routes should be 30/70 preemptible/reserved. document default budgets.

jonathan: I'll run a 48h canary with mirror enabled on realtime-chat in us-west2 with hedging window at 1200ms and snapshot size cap 64KB. will post results.

infra-bot: canary started for `realtime-chat` in us-west2 — id=canary-2160723456-jonathan — sampling 2% traffic.

maya: perfect. please tag me on the postmortem if we see any double-charges or capacity storms.

kevin: one last thought — if the provider exposes a longer reclamation ETA in some regions, prefer mirror+promote there and only hedge in others. region-aware policy.

jonathan: got it. kicking off load tests now, will capture cost delta and p99 improvement.

maya: thanks everyone. short-term goal = reduce p99 > 2s for critical routes without >3% reserved cost delta.

sre-oncall: noted. alerting set for mirror.promote.failed and reserved.pool.hedge_spike.

maya: end."
